findings.title: Switching span-buffer keys from sets to sorted sets breaks existing Redis data and rolling deploys
findings.body: The buffer still uses the existing `span-buf:s:...` key namespace, but now writes with `zadd` and reads with `zscan`/`zcard`. Any keys created by the previous version are Redis sets, not sorted sets. During an upgrade or rolling deploy, processing a batch that touches an existing set key raises a Redis `WRONGTYPE` error at this `p.zadd` or in `add-buffer.lua`; batches then fail and in-flight segments can be lost until those keys expire. The key type change needs a new key namespace/version or an explicit drain/migration before deployment.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields used by audit logs
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` now uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the model value and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime`, so the first non-empty page raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`; even if that were fixed, `build_queryset` would compare a datetime column to an integer. The paginator needs the same timestamp conversion as `DateTimePaginator` or should subclass it.

findings.title: Negative offsets in OptimizedCursorPaginator are passed to Django querysets and raise ValueError
findings.body: The advanced branch accepts a client-supplied negative cursor offset and slices the queryset with it. Django querysets reject negative indexes (`Negative indexing is not supported`), and `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets, so a request with a cursor containing `:-1:0` reaches this line and returns a 500 instead of performing reverse pagination. The same problem remains in the `cursor.is_prev` path at line 182. Negative offsets should be validated/rejected or implemented without negative ORM slicing.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is no longer enforced; eviction cap is hardcoded in Lua
findings.body: The previous `_load_segment_data` check that skipped a segment once it exceeded `self.max_segment_spans` was removed and is not replaced on the Python side. The only cap is now the literal `1000` in `add-buffer.lua`, so `SpansBuffer(max_segment_spans=...)` has no effect, and deployments that configured a different limit silently keep/evict up to 1000 spans without the old `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric. Either pass the configurable limit into the Lua path or remove the parameter and update callers/tests.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit was silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop resolving parent redirects now stops after 1000 hops. For a segment tree deeper than 1000, the script writes a redirect to that truncated ancestor and merges spans into a non-root buffer, causing incorrectly split/merged segments. The previous limit was 10000 and had an explanatory comment; this behavior change is unrelated to eviction and has no covering test.

findings.title: No test covers the new zset eviction behavior
findings.body: The changed tests only add the required `end_timestamp_precise` argument to existing `Span` constructions. They never ingest more than 1000 spans into a segment or assert which spans are evicted, so the new `zpopmin` cap, eviction ordering, and root-span retention are untested. Add a case with more than 1000 spans and explicitly verify the cap and evicted members.
